title: Two-Phase Commit (2PC) and Orphaned Prepared Transaction Disasters
realWorldScenario: An external microservice coordinator used PostgreSQL Two-Phase Commit (`PREPARE TRANSACTION`) to coordinate loan disbursements across a banking ledger and core PostgreSQL. The coordinator service crashed midway. Days later, table bloat explodes and autovacuum is paralyzed.
questionStatement: Explain Two-Phase Commit (2PC) in PostgreSQL (`PREPARE TRANSACTION` and `COMMIT PREPARED`). What happens when a prepared transaction is orphaned? Why do orphaned prepared transactions lock table rows indefinitely and prevent VACUUM from freezing dead tuples across the entire database?

symptoms: Autovacuum unable to clean dead rows
Table and index bloat increasing by 15 GB/day
pg_prepared_xacts shows transaction open for 14 days

systemTelemetry.logSnippet:
2026-11-01 03:00:00 UTC [102]: [1-1] WARNING:  oldest active transaction id is 981204, held by prepared transaction "disburse_loan_49102"
2026-11-01 03:00:00 UTC [102]: [2-1] DETAIL:  Transaction prepared 340 hours ago.

candidateTasks: Explain why prepared transactions survive client disconnects and server restarts
Analyze how an orphaned 2PC holds back the global xmin horizon
Execute ROLLBACK PREPARED to recover the database

expectedConcepts: Prepared transactions surviving client disconnection and server restarts
Holding back catalog xmin horizon and preventing VACUUM across the entire database
hints: Does a prepared transaction abort when the client connection closes?
What catalog table lists all open prepared transactions?
Why does an old transaction ID prevent VACUUM from removing dead rows anywhere?
